cs.t: I had an iPad that Appled forced into obsolecence. I had to throw a perfectly ok piece of hardware on the trash because it was madr unusable by the manufacturer. It's the main reason I despise Apple, including its hardware. I replaced it with a Samsung A7. It's even better than the iPad as I could sideload a manga reader that syncs with Komga, amazing stuff to read manga. And I can install LineageOS if need be. Objectively a better choice than iPad for me.
cs.th: If Apple makes an iPad Neo, it's all over

cs.t: I'm also a premium subscriber, and have struggled with the same issues on the iPad app. I try to keep some shows downloaded for my toddler, and the download feature never seems to work on the first try. I finally got so fed up, I bought a Samsung Galaxy Tab A7 off ebay for $50 and flashed it with LineageOS. I can now load whatever media I want onto the 1 TB sdcard I've installed in it. The 5 year old hardware plays videos just fine with the VLC app. And, as a bonus, I discovered that NewPipe, an alternative YouTube client I installed through the F-Droid store, is actually much more reliable at downloading videos than the official client. I was planning on using yt-dlp to load up the sdcard, but now I don't even need to do that.
cs.th: Yt-dlp: Upcoming new requirements for YouTube downloads

cs.t: My system, which I  absolutely do not recommend on account of numerous failures , is a Samsung 9" Tab A and a Logitech Bluetooth Keyboard.  The keyboard has its own battery, and ~3 months runtime under very constant daily use. If you  can  find a Bluetooth keyboard your Kobo will talk to, I'd strongly recommend it, and please tell me your experiences. In theory, this is a very attractive system, and in terms of the hardware and physical aspects, it is.  The vendor support, OS, applications, and durability, however, are not. 1. Samsung locks down the Tab A hard, and I've been unable to root or ROM it. I'd like to do both.  Given other direct and indirect experiences with Samsung, my advice is to steer clear of the company and its products for the next decade or two.  It simply cannot execute and doesn't care about customer experience. 2. The Logitech mouse/case is attractive, and the form factor is excellent.  But the keyboard itself is shedding keys and Logitec claims it has no viable replacement (that is:  the keyboard model is hard-paired with this specific device, and discontinued).  That after about six weeks of absolutely failing to comprehend the problem at hand, and pretty much straight-up lying about the problem.  I've an as-yet-untested promise for a refund should I find a viable replacement keyboard, but cannot find anything that is the same lap-stable folio-type case-keyboard combination. There are some very bad key placements - the "app" key is between "fn" and "a
cs.th: How I Kicked My Smartphone Addiction, and Never Looked Back
